status: Unreleased QuickJS heap-transfer foundation. Public SDK/runtime 0.19.2 and production deployment are unchanged; contexts.create/get/list/reset/delete remain unimplemented.
runtime: Native Alchemy workerd and R2; original Worker closed before replacement. No JSON reconstruction of globals or program replay.
nativeChecks: A Rust QuickJS Guest pauses at a real host callback and transfers its opaque heap through content-addressed native R2 objects.
A fresh Worker restores the pending Promise, lexical closure, global counter and captured output; one entered marker, result 43 and exit 0.
A corrupted heap fails integrity validation before native resume.
A different Rust binary revision fails with CHECKPOINT_RUNTIME_MISMATCH.
A runtime that previously created and freed another Guest cannot park a new Guest; Rust checks the total constructor-attempt count.

unpublishedRuntimeCandidate.scope: Private candidate archives for local compatibility checks only. They do not replace the published 0.19.2 assets.

packageProof.transport: native Alchemy workerd service binding and Agent RPC; local R2 and Queue
packageProof.proof: SDK archive exports and consumer declarations; runtime archive; filesystem snapshot restore; hard-link metadata; RPC callbacks and cooperative disposal; ephemeral context disposal with 1024 files and concurrent closes; persistent driver contexts and cancellation; scoped authority

minuteiProof.transport: native workerd Agent service binding; actual Minutei Code Mode and tenant SQLite; local R2, KV and Queue

openBoundaries: Context API admission and concurrent-operation ownership.
Reentry for another operation in the retained language context, including module/cache semantics.
Reset/delete, interruption, expiry and current-authority enforcement.
Python retained globals and heap restoration.
Paged production persistence, migration/runtime-upgrade policy and garbage collection.
Real production proof and performance/billing measurements.
limits: The native fixture uses one bounded whole-heap R2 blob to establish transfer feasibility, not a production checkpoint algorithm.
Only same-binary cooperative QuickJS continuation is proved; arbitrary crash, external-effect replay and cross-build migration are not proved.
The public Context API is not implemented by this checkpoint primitive.
